That's some ugly hack.
Is there no way to avoid having a special case for the debugger? It looks like something that will stay after dock refactoring, unless you have some replacement in mind that isn't possible already?
You could change that into early return.

It would work as an early return, but wouldn't that hinder future changes to the function? I was under the impression that input functions shouldn't use early returns because not every input is treated the same. I suppose that with this function it is alright because it probably won't be needed for any other use case
This can crash if item is not found.

Well the benefit is that the debugger manages itself this way, so you don't have a special case for a dock.
Though some more universal solution would be nice. What if a user runs into the same problem with their plugin?

Maybe this could be included as a toggle in the EditorDock? Since it extends MarginContainer like the DebuggerNode currently does.

Note that the main thing the current workaround in bottompanel does is to give the panel a negative extended margin, and to make the debuggernode fill the entire panel (because the debugger node has its own margins and it doesn't want to double up).

Thinking about that, it could still be in BottomPanel but more generally for making the dock fill the entire panel. Like an invisible panel that has zero margin.

Why does debugger have margins? If they are the same as in bottom panel, maybe the should be removed?
Or, you could add a special case for MarginContainer and cancel out its margins maybe. Still hacky, but at least not towards single dock.

For reference, this is what the debugger would look like if there was no exception made for the debugger node. The BottomPanel applies margins to the DebuggerNode, which looks bad (and pushes the debugger node up). Ideally, the docks should not have any margin and let the EditorDock class handle that, but for the moment I think that the current hack is the least amount of code to address this without the EditorDock class. I'd be willing to do this for anything extending MarginContainer though.
